text: {"headline":"Provider 1000000127 bills 99215 at roughly four times the risk-adjusted expectation at every complexity level, but documentation is too thin to separate upcoding from a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The elevated 99215 share shows up in every complexity band, including patients with zero or one chronic condition. The sampled low-complexity 99215 claims include single-problem visits such as C0082961 (J06.9 only), C0082918 (N39.0) and C0083885 (R10.9). That pattern is consistent with level inflation rather than with complexity alone, although the high-complexity sample (e.g., C0082857, C0083212) does reflect a genuinely multimorbid subset. The records review cuts the other way but is very thin: all five documented 99215 claims were supported at high MDM (e.g., C0083376, C0084180). Two 99214 notes were documented at low MDM (C0083403, C0083591), a rate somewhat above peers on a small base. The four moderate-plus data-reviewed notes with no lab or test line are weak evidence of templated or inflated documentation, not proof. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims listed in the packet and check whether the notes support high MDM or qualifying time, and whether they look cloned across visits."}
